title: Idempotent-complete triangulation
statement:
The scalar operation of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is independent of $N$
and of the representative of $f$ and makes $\mathcal P_T=\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$
$\Qlb$-linear. The shift and distinguished triangles of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] give $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ the structure of an
idempotent-complete ordinary triangulated category, and the canonical
functor $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)\to\Kar(\Dbc(T,\Qlb))$ is an exact equivalence. For
every finite $E$ the composite
$$
 \Dbc(T,E)\xrightarrow{j_E}\mathcal P_T=\Dbc(T,\Qlb)
$$
is exact and $E$-linear.

05R6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05R6)), and the Karoubianity
criterion Lemma 13.4.14 ([Tag
05QW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QW)). Difference: all of these
live in one additive category over one fixed coefficient ring, whereas the
statement here concerns the filtered colimit $\mathcal P_T$ with its
$\Qlb$-scalar action.

proof.text: Work with the prime, algebraic closure and noetherian finite-dimensional scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible fixed in [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. The finite-stage Hom modules of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] have their usual scalar action, and composition on the raw scalar localization is bilinear by [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. We first check the scalar identity needed for transport. The functors and associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] are the specified derived change of completed coefficient rings followed by scalar localization. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the integral change of rings is computed on K-flat complexes. For $b\in\mathcal O_M$, the chain map $b\,\mathrm{id}$ is sent under tensor to $b\,\mathrm{id}$, since $(bx)\otimes y=x\otimes by$. This identity survives passage to the derived category and scalar localization. Writing $c=b/\varpi_M^r\in M$ gives $T_{N/M}(c\,\mathrm{id})=c\,\mathrm{id}$, and functoriality then gives $T_{N/M}(cu)=cT_{N/M}(u)$. Each component of the associator is a morphism over its target field, so composing it with $c\,\mathrm{id}$ commutes with scalar multiplication. Consequently the pair-category transport satisfies $(cu)_N=c\,u_N$ whenever $c\in M\subseteq N$.

source.place: Proof, scalar-transport justification expanded before the first sentence

proof.text: Fix $f=[M,u]$ and $\alpha\in\Qlb$. The definition [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] permits a finite stage $N$ containing $M$ and $\Ql(\alpha)$. For two such choices $N,N'$, take their compositum $P$. By the transport transitivity in [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] and the scalar identity in step 1, $(\alpha u_N)_P=\alpha u_P=(\alpha u_{N'})_P$. The equivalence relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] therefore identifies the two prescribed classes. If $[M,u]=[M',v]$, that definition supplies a finite $R$ with $u_R=v_R$. Enlarge $R$ to contain $\Ql(\alpha)$ and both stages chosen to multiply the two representatives. Transport transitivity gives equality there, and multiplying by $\alpha$ preserves it. Thus the prescription is independent both of the auxiliary field and of the representative.

source.place: Proof, independence of N and of the representative

proof.text: For any proposed module law or bilinearity identity, choose one finite field containing all coefficient fields of the finitely many morphisms and all scalars appearing. This is possible by the compositum construction in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. Use [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] to compute the additions and composites there, and step 1 to compute all scalar products there. In the localized Hom modules of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], with composition as in [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], the equalities $1u=u$, $0u=0$, $(\alpha\beta)u=\alpha(\beta u)$, $(\alpha+\beta)u=\alpha u+\beta u$, $\alpha(u+v)=\alpha u+\alpha v$, and $(\alpha v)\circ u=\alpha(v\circ u)=v\circ(\alpha u)$ hold. Passing to classes proves the module axioms and bilinearity. The underlying additive category is already supplied by the common-stage calculus. These are exactly the requirements of [def-weil-linear-category], so $\mathcal P_T$ is $\Qlb$-linear.

source.place: Proof, field laws and bilinearity at a common stage

proof.text: The shift and distinguished triangles in [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] are precisely the common-stage shift and cone triangles. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms] to these data: it states all four Verdier axioms, including the octahedral axiom, and states exactness of every $j_E$ with its specified shift comparison. Thus the triangulation asserted here is an ordinary triangulation on the category already equipped with the scalar action of steps 1--3.

Apply [thm-weil-pbc-qbar-idempotent-complete] to this same category, without changing the raw common-stage model: its statement gives idempotent completeness and says explicitly that the canonical fully faithful inclusion into the envelope [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] is an exact equivalence. This supplies both remaining assertions. In particular exactness is taken from that theorem, rather than inferred merely from an equivalence of underlying categories.

source.place: Proof, idempotent completeness and the canonical exact equivalence

proof.text: For a finite stage $E$, the functor $j_E$ sends $K$ to $(E,K)$ and $u$ to $[E,u]$ in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. The source category $\Dbc(T,E)$ has its $E$-module Hom structure from [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] and [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. For $\alpha\in E$ the scalar prescription of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] may use $N=E$, since $T_{E/E}=\mathrm{id}$. Hence $\alpha j_E(u)=[E,\alpha u]=j_E(\alpha u)$. Likewise $j_E(u+v)=[E,u+v]=[E,u]+[E,v]$. These are precisely the conditions of [def-weil-linear-functor], using restriction of the target scalar action from $\Qlb$ to $E$. Together with exactness from step 4, they prove the final clause.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: exactness and E-linearity of j_E

blueprint_update.statement:
The scalar operation of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is independent of $N$
and of the representative of $f$ and makes $\mathcal P_T=\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$
$\Qlb$-linear. The shift and distinguished triangles of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] give $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ the structure of an
idempotent-complete ordinary triangulated category, and the canonical
functor $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)\to\Kar(\Dbc(T,\Qlb))$ is an exact equivalence. For
every finite $E$ the composite
$$
 \Dbc(T,E)\xrightarrow{j_E}\mathcal P_T=\Dbc(T,\Qlb)
$$
is exact and $E$-linear.

proof.text:
The scalar operation of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is independent of $N$:
for two finite fields $N,N'$ containing $\Ql(\alpha)$ and the stage $M$, the
representatives $\alpha u_N$ and $\alpha u_{N'}$ transport to their
compositum and agree there, since $T_{P/N}$ and $T_{P/N'}$ are linear over
$N$ and $N'$ (hence over $N\cap N'$ containing $\Ql(\alpha)$); independence
of the representative of $f$ holds through the representative equivalence
relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]: transport an equality
$u_P=v_P$, which survives scalar multiplication. The field laws and
bilinearity hold at a common stage by
[prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], so $\mathcal P_T$ is $\Qlb$-linear.
By [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms], $\mathcal P_T=\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ is
triangulated, and it is idempotent complete by
[thm-weil-pbc-qbar-idempotent-complete], so the canonical fully faithful
functor into the Karoubi envelope is an equivalence by that theorem, hence
exact. The composite $j_E$ is exact by [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms], and
$E$-linear and $\Qlb$-linear by the displayed scalar definition.
